brief: c298: `freeBay()` starves its index-0 bay. On HEAD, over six seeds x a year, house 1 took 0.35-0.75% of daylight samples to house 7's 4.9% — a 7x gap on a terrace whose whole promise is that it is somebody's (probes/terrace-presence.mjs measured it and is on disk). #201's filter evened it by accident and the branch was never examined, so nobody knows whether the bias is in freeBay(k,want)'s scan order, in leadsKit(bay)'s furnishing, or in spawnTenant's choice of house. Find which, fix it at the one place it lives, and re-run the probe. This is the domain's SECOND iteration ever and its whole surface is 20% of the wide frame and ~34% of the phone's, so a tenant who is only ever on one end of it is a visible fault, not a statistical one.
successLooksLike: probes/terrace-presence.mjs over the same six seeds x a year shows the per-house daylight-presence spread inside a factor of ~2 rather than 7x, with the total presence unchanged — this is a redistribution, not more tenants. Census byte-identical to HEAD if no behaviour but the choice moved.
avoid: Do not raise TEN_CAP or TEN_STAND to paper over it — the cap is not the fault and a raised cap hides the diagnosis. If the measurement says the gap is by construction and correct, say so and close the cue: a killed premise is a good iteration.
